articles.title: Duleep Trophy Final: East Zone finish day 1 on 385/4 as Ishan Kishan remains unbeaten on 111
articles.summary: Cricket News: Ishan Kishan led from the front with a superb unbeaten century as East Zone finished Day 1 of the Duleep Trophy 2026 final on 385/4 against South Zone.
articles.body: Ishan Kishan led from the front with a superb unbeaten century as East Zone finished Day 1 of the Duleep Trophy 2026 final on 385/4 against South Zone at the MA Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai on Sunday.After winning the toss and opting to bat, Kishan anchored a strong batting display from East Zone, scoring 111 not out off 135 balls. His innings featured 14 fours and two sixes as he took control of the contest in the final session.Kishan found an excellent partner in Kumar Kushagra, who remained unbeaten on 63 off 75 balls. The pair added an unbeaten 144-run partnership for the fifth wicket off 160 balls, completely taking the game away from South Zone towards the end of the day.Kishan takes charge after Mohan fallsEast Zone made a solid start through Abhimanyu Easwaran (72) and teenage batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (44). Easwaran and Sooryavanshi gave the side a strong platform before both departed. Sudip Kumar Gharami was then dismissed for 6, bringing Shikhar Mohan to the crease. Mohan played a composed knock of 85 off 120 balls, helping East Zone build another important partnership before Chama Milind ended his innings at 241/4.That dismissal brought Kishan and Kushagra together, and the pair ensured there were no further setbacks.Kishan accelerated as the innings progressed and brought up his century in style, remaining unbeaten at the close. His knock was particularly important given his role as captain, with East Zone now firmly in control after the opening day.South Zone struggle for breakthroughsSouth Zone's bowling attack found little assistance from a placid batting surface, while the bowlers also struggled with consistency. Chama Milind was the most successful bowler, finishing the day with figures of 2/56 from 13 overs. Tripurana Vijay picked up one wicket but conceded 114 runs from his 22 overs.Mohammed Siraj, meanwhile, went wicketless despite bowling 14 overs and conceded 96 runs. East Zone also benefited from a late surge, scoring 74 runs without losing a wicket in the final 10 overs. Kishan and Kushagra's partnership allowed them to finish the day strongly at 385/4.With Kishan unbeaten on 111 and Kushagra on 63, East Zone will resume on Day 2 with an opportunity to push towards a total of 400 and beyond. South Zone, meanwhile, will desperately need early wickets with the second new ball to prevent East Zone from building an even bigger first-innings total.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Title-chasing Nottinghamshire lose Kyle Verreynne ahead of crucial County Championship run-in
articles.summary: Cricket News: Nottinghamshire’s County Championship title push has suffered a blow after South Africa wicketkeeper-batter Kyle Verreynne was recalled early by Crick.
articles.body: Nottinghamshire’s County Championship title push has suffered a blow after South Africa wicketkeeper-batter Kyle Verreynne was recalled early by Cricket South Africa, ruling him out of the club’s final three matches of the season.Verreynne, 29, is in his third stint with Nottinghamshire and had initially agreed to play in all of the club’s red-ball fixtures this summer. However, his central contract commitments with South Africa take priority as the Proteas prepare for a three-Test home series against Australia.His final appearance for Nottinghamshire this season will come against Leicestershire at Trent Bridge, before he returns to South Africa.Verreynne departure comes at crucial stageVerreynne’s departure comes at a crucial stage of Nottinghamshire’s campaign. They currently sit second in the County Championship, four points behind leaders Somerset and one point ahead of third-placed Warwickshire, with just three rounds remaining.The club will now have to manage the final stretch of the title race without their first-choice wicketkeeper, with fixtures against Hampshire, Sussex and Yorkshire still to come.Despite his early departure, Verreynne said he would continue to follow Nottinghamshire’s title challenge closely.“I think I've said it so many times, the club's got a really special place. It's got a special place to me, so I'll be watching closely.”He added:“The team's in a good position at the moment, playing some really good cricket. I think it's going to be quite an exciting run-in, so I'll be keeping a close eye.”Mick Newell acknowledges CSA’s decisionNottinghamshire Director of Cricket Mick Newell admitted that losing Verreynne at this point of the season was far from ideal, although the club understood South Africa’s position.“It’s not ideal that we’re losing Kyle at this point in the season, but we understand the decision made by Cricket South Africa, and he returns with our best wishes for a busy winter.”Newell also praised Verreynne’s contribution during his latest spell with the club, saying his performances had helped Nottinghamshire put themselves in a strong position heading into the final weeks of the Championship.“We’ve been very happy to have Kyle with us for most of the summer, during which his contributions have put us in a strong position as we head towards the final few matches,” he said.With several South African players being recalled from county cricket ahead of the Australia series, Nottinghamshire will now look for a replacement for Verreynne.“There’s always a lot of hard work being done behind the scenes to make sure we’re prepared for every outcome, and we hope to confirm a replacement for Kyle as soon as we’re able to,” Newell added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: England clinch ODI series sweep of Ireland as Sophia Dunkley hits second international century in 114-run win
articles.summary: England collapse from 260-4 to 291 all out after Sophia Dunkley (119 off 119 balls) hits run-a-ball century, but Ireland fail to threaten in run-chase; Lauren Filer (3-27), Mady Villiers (3-33) and Tilly Corteen-Coleman (2-34) impress as tourists are skittled for 177
articles.body:
Sophia Dunkley (119 off 119 balls) struck a run-a-ball century - her second in ODI cricket - as England set Ireland 292 to win, having been inserted by the visitors.

But Ireland never truly threatened in reply, despite a handful of starts for their top-order batters, as they were ultimately bowled out for 177 after 44.2 overs.

England were also bowled out short of their allotted 50 overs, as the hosts collapsed from 183-1 in the 31st over and 260-4 in the 43rd to 291 all out after 48.5.

It wouldn't prove costly, however, as Lauren Filer (3-27), Mady Villiers (3-33) and Tilly Corteen-Coleman (2-34) starred with the ball to skittle Ireland and secure a series whitewash.

Dunkley continued her fine form with the bat this summer as she cracked 15 boundaries in her sublime knock, sharing in a 73-run opening partnership with Maia Bouchier and dominating a second-wicket century stand with Jodi Grewcock (35).

It laid the foundation for what looked set to be a sizeable score of around 350 or beyond, only for things to fall apart at the back end.

Alice Capsey (10) was run out cheaply, before Dunkley holed out in the deep, and though Dani Gibson (41 off 37) and Freya Kemp (23 off 21) cracked a few lusty blows in a 46-run partnership for the fifth wicket, England lost 6-31 in the space of little more than six overs thereafter.

Ireland captain Gaby Lewis claimed a terrific catch on the long-off boundary to see the back of Kemp and trigger the collapse, with leg-spinner Cara Murray (4-56) claiming a career-first four-for.

Filer (16) dismissed Lewis early on in the Ireland reply, before Alice Tector (29) and Amy Hunter (39) laid the foundations with a 56-run second-wicket stand - but too slowly.

The tourists began to fall behind the required rate, and there was only to be one winner when the wickets began to tumble.

Corteen-Coleman first bowled Tector, Capsey then claimed a couple of stumpings - Hunter and Rebecca Stokell (14) - to continue her successful wicketkeeping audition in this series, before Orla Prendergast (24) was caught at deep midwicket.

Corteen-Coleman then cleaned up another batter, Louise Little (14), as Ireland lost their last five wickets for 10 runs in under four overs - Filer finishing off the job by dismantling Kia McCartney's stumps.

Player of the series and match Sophia Dunkley:

"It was just great to get the series win today.

"It was definitely tricky at the start. The longer you batted the easier it got. It was nice to get through that period and see us home.

"For me, it is just about staying really present. I love batting for whatever team I am playing for and it is great to be at the top of the order again in ODI cricket.

"It is definitely my goal to be at the top of the order in all formats."

"We all know she can get off to fast and furious starts. The main goal for her this series will have been match-winning contributions.

"She wanted big runs and she has done that today."

First ODI (Leicester) - England win by six wickets

Second ODI (Derby) - England win by six wickets

Third ODI (Worcester) - England win by 114 runs

articles.title: England v Ireland: Sophia Dunkley cetury seals hosts' dominant series clean sweep
articles.summary: Sophia Dunkley hits 119 as England end their international summer with a 114-run thrashing of Ireland at Worcester.
articles.body:
England 291 (48.5 overs): Dunkley 119 (119); Murray 4-56

Ireland 177 (44.2 overs): Hunter 39 (58); Filer 3-27

Sophia Dunkley's sparkling century led England to a comprehensive 114-run win in the third and final one-day international against Ireland at Worcester.

Dunkley's run-a-ball 119 set up England's 291 before Ireland were bowled out for 177 in 44.2 overs, sealing a 3-0 clean sweep for Charlie Dean's side.

England were eyeing a record total after opener Dunkley's second international century, but the innings fell away from 260-4 and they frustratingly lost their last six wickets for just 31 runs to be dismissed with seven balls unused.

Dunkley added 73 for the first wicket with Maia Bouchier, who continued her fine run of form with 39, before Jodi Grewcock also wasted a good start as she was caught and bowled for 35 and Alice Capsey was unlucky to be run out backing up for 10.

All-rounders Freya Kemp and Dani Gibson threatened to push England beyond 300 but it was the former's wicket that kickstarted the collapse as she was caught at long-on for 23 and a run of single-figure scores followed, though Gibson kicked on to an ODI-best 41.

Leg-spinner Cara Murray was the pick of Ireland's bowlers with 4-56 as the visitors fought back admirably, and England only managed to hit seven boundaries after Dunkley's departure in the 36th over.

Despite the disappointing end to the innings, England still had plenty on the board in another non-contest between bat and ball.

Amy Hunter top-scored with 39 but no Irish batter was able to score at a strike-rate above 100 and the run-rate spiralled beyond their grasp, as Mady Villiers and Lauren Filer took three wickets apiece.

The final match of the series concludes England's international summer. Their next confirmed games will come at the Champions Trophy in February, though a multi-format series against West Indies in the autumn and three ODIs against Sri Lanka are in the schedule, but the dates have not been released.

Ireland women in England 2026 Published 1 hour ago

This has been a series with an unusual context for England.

Key stars such as Lauren Bell, Sophie Ecclestone and Nat Sciver-Brunt have been rested, which has presented opportunities to experiment with the likes of fringe players in Grewcock and Tilly Corteen-Coleman.

But the curious cricketing calendar means they have few opportunities to play the format, with the autumn schedule still unconfirmed and their next home ODI coming in the Ashes next summer, meaning they have been simultaneously seeking stability.

The opening partnership was one question that needed answering after Tammy Beaumont's retirement earlier this year, and a century apiece for Dunkley and Bouchier in this series has seen them take their chance.

Of course, Ireland's bowling attack is incomparable to Australia's and to cite this as Ashes preparation would be very unrealistic, but England can only play the schedule they are given.

Dunkley had been threatening in the first two games, falling for 73 at Leicester before she was stitched up by Bouchier's poor running at Derby - but she was not to be denied a third time.

The 28-year-old started patiently, reaching her half-century off 63 balls after Bouchier dominated the strike early on, before kicking on and whacking her next fifty off just 37.

A notable change to her game has been her improvement through the off-side, scoring her runs almost equally split across both sides of the wicket - a big change for a player previously known for her leg-side dominance.

Ireland tested her with the short ball and forced her to hit to the sweepers, which she handled efficiently before her eventual downfall as she was brilliantly caught by Prendergast at deep square leg.

Sciver-Brunt is likely to slot straight back in at number three, and England have a decision to make about whether Capsey keeps the gloves over Amy Jones, but for now, Dunkley and Bouchier have solved one of coach Charlotte Edwards' headaches.

The series was also a valuable opportunity for England's crop of seamers to test themselves without Bell leading the attack, another area of their squad that needed strengthening.

With spinners dominating the T20 World Cup earlier this summer, the likes of Filer and Issy Wong were sidelined, but both have stepped up admirably.

Wong starred in the second ODI with her first international five-wicket haul before resting for this final game where Filer troubled the Irish batters throughout with her lively pace, which helped her take 3-27.

Contrastingly, Ryana Macdonald-Gay offered a change of tempo with her niggly medium-pace and Edwards will be hoping for Kemp to return to bowling fitness soon in order to give herself another option in the middle overs alongside Gibson.

Villiers took 3-33 with her off-spin as she claimed the big wickets of Hunter and Orla Prendergast, and with Corteen-Coleman waiting in Ecclestone's wings, England's bowling stocks are in a healthy position.

Ireland barely threatened to reach their target, with captain Gaby Lewis falling early for 16 to dent their hopes almost immediately and fellow opener Alice Tector trudged to 29 off 59 balls, which saw the run-rate climb steadily.

England were made to work hard for their wickets throughout a stalling middle-over phase but eventually they ripped through the lower order with Ireland's last five wickets falling in a heap for just 10 runs.

articles.title: 'Bhaiya gave me a lot of advice': Shikhar Mohan’s 85 gives East Zone a lift; Reveals Ishan Kishan’s guidance
articles.summary: Cricket News: Shikhar Mohan, Jharkhand batter credited captain Ishan Kishan’s constant guidance after making an impressive 85 on his Duleep Trophy debut against Sou.
articles.body: Shikhar Mohan, Jharkhand batter credited captain Ishan Kishan’s constant guidance after making an impressive 85 on his Duleep Trophy debut against South Zone in the 2026/27 final.Mohan, who came into the East Zone XI as a replacement for Jharkhand teammate Virat Singh, played a key role in rebuilding the innings after the early wickets. He added 94 runs for the third wicket with Kishan, helping East Zone recover and take control on the opening day.Kishan remained unbeaten on 111 at stumps, while Kumar Kushagra was not out on 63 as East Zone finished the day on 385/4 in 79 overs.“Ishan bhaiya was giving me a lot of advice while batting. He was telling me what shot is on and what is not. Thanks to that, we had a great partnership,” Mohan told reporters after play.Ranji form and T20 experience boost debutMohan earned his place in the East Zone side after an outstanding debut Ranji Trophy season, where he scored 613 runs at an average of 55.72. Although primarily an opener, he had no issues adapting to the No. 3 position with Abhimanyu Easwaran and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi opening for East Zone.“My journey has been very good so far. My first season in Ranji Trophy went very well, so coming into this match, I just wanted to carry that forward. I was looking to maintain that form from the Ranji Trophy,” he said.Mohan also accepted the challenge of facing South Zone’s short-ball strategy, with five fielders stationed on the leg side. He showed patience before eventually falling to Chama Milind after an inside edge off a bouncer.“The plan was that I would leave the ball first, and when they get tired, they will give me chances to score runs. I made a poor decision and got out,” he admitted.The youngster also felt his experience in the Jharkhand T20 League helped him handle the pressure of playing in front of a sizeable crowd at the MA Chidambaram Stadium.“I think it helped a lot. The crowds there were also very good, so today when there was a big crowd, it felt normal to me,” Mohan said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Jordan Hermann, bowlers shine as South Africa beat Zimbabwe to clinch tri-series title
articles.summary: Cricket News: South Africa produced a strong all-round performance to beat Zimbabwe by 48 runs in the final and win the T20I tri-series at the Namibia Cricket Groun.
articles.body: South Africa produced a strong all-round performance to beat Zimbabwe by 48 runs in the final and win the T20I tri-series at the Namibia Cricket Ground on Sunday.Batting first, South Africa posted 205/5 in 20 overs after choosing to bat. Jordan Hermann led the way with a quick half-century, while Dewald Brevis and Rubin Hermann also made important contributions.Zimbabwe struggled from the start in the chase and were bowled out for 157 in 18 overs.Hermann gives South Africa a flying startSouth Africa were without opener Lhuan-dre Pretorius, who missed the final with a niggle. But his absence did not affect the team's start.Jordan Hermann attacked the Zimbabwe bowlers from the beginning and reached his fifty in just 24 balls. His innings included eight fours and a six.He added 84 runs for the opening wicket with Connor Esterhuizen, who scored 32.Brevis then kept the pressure on Zimbabwe in the middle overs. He scored 32 from 23 balls, hitting two fours and two sixes.Rubin Hermann added 27 off 16 balls, with three fours and a six. His partnership with Brevis helped South Africa cross the 200-run mark.Brad Evans and Newman Nyamhuri took two wickets each for Zimbabwe, but South Africa finished with a big total of 205/5.Zimbabwe lose wickets earlyZimbabwe needed 206 runs to win but suffered a terrible start.Ben Curran was dismissed for a first-ball duck by Eathan Bosch. Duan Jansen and Bosch then continued to trouble the Zimbabwe batters as four wickets fell inside the powerplay.Captain Sikandar Raza got a second chance when a caught-behind decision against him was overturned because Bosch had bowled a no-ball.However, South Africa captain Bjorn Fortuin soon ended Raza's stay at the crease. He finished with three wickets for 24 runs as Zimbabwe's chase fell apart.Evans fights back but Zimbabwe fall shortBrad Evans gave Zimbabwe some hope late in the innings.The pacer scored his maiden T20I half-century and put on 52 runs for the ninth wicket with Kundai Matigimu.But Kwena Maphaka broke the partnership, and Zimbabwe were eventually bowled out in the 18th over.Duan Jansen was South Africa's best bowler, finishing with 3/38, while Bosch took 2/22.It was South Africa's third win over Zimbabwe in just eight days.Important preparation for 2027 World CupThe tri-series was an important preparation tournament for South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, who will co-host the 2027 ICC Cricket World Cup.South Africa will now play a three-match ODI series against Namibia. Fortuin will continue to lead the team in the series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Shubman Gill loses his wicket to CSK's intern bowler in his first match of Sher-e-Punjab T20 league
articles.summary: While fans expected Arshdeep Singh to be Shubman Gill's arch-nemesis in the Sher-e-Punjab Trophy, instead it is a CSK intern bowler who took his wicket.
articles.body:
Shubman Gill was dismissed for 40 by Kartik Chadha in his first Sher-e-Punjab T20 match.

Chadha served as Chennai Super Kings' intern bowler during the IPL 2025 season.

The India skipper struck seven fours and a six in a quickfire 21-ball knock for the Fazilka Falcons.

Kartik Chadha surprises Shubman Gill as he dismisses the India skipper in Sher-e-Punjab T20

Shubman Gill finally took the field for Fazilka Falcons in the Sher-e-Punjab T20 League on Saturday, and his first outing as captain produced fireworks with the bat before ending at the hands of one of CSK's own. Kartik Chadha, who spent IPL 2025 as CSK's intern bowler, dismissed the India captain for a blistering 40 off 21 balls.

Gill had been absent for the Falcons' first four matches of the tournament, with the side losing three of them as he attended the BCCI's performance review meeting in Mumbai. His arrival was the most anticipated moment of the league's season so far.

The India skipper wasted no time finding his rhythm, opening the innings and striking seven fours and a six before Chadha's leg-spin ended his cameo. The Falcons were eventually set a target they could not overcome.

Who is Kartik Chadha, the CSK intern who dismissed Shubman Gill?

Chadha is a 21-year-old right-arm leg-spinner and left-handed middle-order batter from Jalandhar, a product of CT Public School who has quietly built an impressive résumé through Punjab's age-group system.

His numbers across domestic youth cricket are striking. During the 2021-22 Under-19 Punjab tournament, Chadha emerged as the highest wicket-taker with 36 wickets in nine matches for Jalandhar district. He represented Punjab in the BCCI's Vijay Merchant Trophy and later topped the Senior One-Day Inter-District Tournament with 16 wickets in six matches.

Those performances caught the attention of Chennai Super Kings, who brought him on board as an intern bowler for the 2025 IPL season. The role gave Chadha access to the franchise's training infrastructure and coaching staff, including the chance to bowl at some of the finest batters in the competition during net sessions.

Dismissing India's Test and ODI captain in a state-level T20 is the most visible return on that investment so far, and it will not have gone unnoticed by the CSK management heading into the IPL 2027 auction cycle.
